bodies.name: Omnigres
bodies.line: Postgres as a Platform.
bodies.desc: Postgres as a complete application runtime: business logic, job queues, API endpoints, an HTTP server — inside or next to the database, instead of a constellation of services. 2022–2025; continued as Inferal (2025).

bodies.name: Strata
bodies.line: A 64-bit machine where memory is explicit I/O.
bodies.desc: A prototype instruction set and the small operating system that proves it. Local Stores instead of caches; transfers that complete with a tag; no interrupts.
bodies.quote: The machine shows through instead of being hidden.
bodies.voice: The machine shows through instead of being hidden.
notes: RTL, a C emulator with JITs, the StrataOS microkernel written in Strata assembly, Strata Forth, and a browser playground.
Local Stores, not caches: 64 KiB per core. Transfers carry completion tags: tget, tput, tany. Linear capabilities.
StrataOS has a tiled window server and a strip of core cells that pulse on context switches — this desktop is its cousin.

bodies.name: libycxx
bodies.line: An independent C++26 standard library.
bodies.desc: Freestanding core plus hosted library; import std; works. Version 0.1.0. Presented as a spec sheet, because that is what it is.
bodies.quote: There is no list of tolerated failures.
bodies.voice: There is no list of tolerated failures.
notes: 2,824 spec-derived tests, plus 17,098 external libc++ and libstdc++ tests run unmodified.
Implemented by AI agents directed by the author.

bodies.name: ycxx
bodies.line: An independent, resident C++26 compiler.
bodies.desc: Preprocessor, front end, constant evaluator, code generator, object writer and linker, all its own. It stays resident, holds the whole program's analysis in memory, and recomputes only what a change can affect.
bodies.quote: How far can we get with this?
bodies.voice: How far can we get with this?
notes: In one week, from an old idea to compiling a good subset of C++ (classes, templates, constant evaluation) to signed macOS arm64 and static x86-64 Linux executables, with no external compiler, assembler or linker.
Watch mode with an interactive trace for people and agents; ycxx policies for affine and linear type checking; its own benchmarking tool.
Built by AI agents directed by the author, like libycxx before it. Open to anyone with spare LLM capacity to point at it.

bodies.name: Flyology
bodies.line: Systems foundations for Ada.
bodies.desc: Named after Flyology, the book Ada Lovelace planned at twelve. Two task lanes, native and lightweight, and the libraries a serious system needs.
notes: Libraries: HTTP, Postgres, QUIC, JSON, RDF, SIMD, TUI, NUMA, Cachelines, Allocators.

bodies.name: lasocket
bodies.line: One IP, many machines answering it at once.
bodies.desc: Active-active TCP and UDP sockets across a LAN. Every node holds every connection; kill nodes, kill the coordinator, replace every machine, and nc, curl and ping sessions keep going, byte-exact.
notes: No coordinator on the hot path: who sends each segment block is a rendezvous hash over the live members, and nothing is acknowledged until two nodes hold it.
Adapts to the switch: multicast, flood or relay per neighbor. No router or switch configuration.
Rust. A Docker demo kills nodes, flips the switch through four scenarios and runs a chaos monkey while clients verify every byte.
